label: Shared COMP101 T-Box (classes + object properties) for vocab diff
comment: Authors may add module-local classes; anything not listed here shows up as only-in-upload. Core merge vocabulary lives here.

classes.comment: A week or unit in the course schedule.
An idea to understand, not a keyword (e.g. Indexing).
A common loop or problem-solving pattern (e.g. Accumulator).
Python surface that can implement or use curriculum concepts (syntax, methods, builtins). Groups LanguageConstruct with invokables for T-box connectivity.
Callable Python API: type-bound methods and global built-in functions.
A Python built-in type used in code (e.g. list, dict).
An exception students may encounter (e.g. IndexError).
Python syntax such as a for loop or the [] operator.
A function bound to a data type (e.g. list.append()).
A global built-in function such as len() or sorted() (adopted from the shared OOP T-Box; cleaner than modelling these as LanguageConstructs).
A learning outcome the student should achieve.

object_properties.comment: Week where an entity is first introduced (primary teaching). Use revisitedIn for reinforcement in a later week.
Week where a concept introduced earlier is reinforced in a new context — not first taught here.
Strict prerequisite: the source should be learned after the target. Transitive, so prerequisite chains close automatically (adopted from the OOP T-Box).
Pedagogical soft ordering: the source is usually taught before the target. Non-transitive; skippable when the learner has already mastered the target.
Syntax-level coding of a concept (LanguageConstruct). BuiltInFunctions use usesConcept instead — do not attach implementsConcept to builtins.

A method, construct, or built-in function relies on / carries out a concept or abstract operation (create, access, remove, ...). Shared name with the OOP module (replaces the earlier performsOperation).
The data type a method or built-in function returns (adopted from the OOP module; richer than the returnsNone boolean, which is kept as a shortcut).
Two entities that students often confuse and should compare (e.g. list vs tuple, shallow vs deep copy). Symmetric; shared with the OOP module.
A method belongs to a type or class. Range widened to owl:Thing to also cover user-defined classes in the OOP module.
An entity can raise this error type.
A skill requires understanding of a concept.
Inverse of taughtIn: a lecture first introduces this entity.
Inverse of revisitedIn: a lecture reinforces this entity from an earlier week.
Inverse of dependsOn: the source is a prerequisite that enables the target.
Inverse of recommendedBefore: the source normally comes later in the teaching sequence.
Inverse of implementsConcept: a concept is coded by this language construct, method, or built-in.
Inverse of usesConcept: this concept/operation is used by the given method, construct, or built-in function.
Inverse of producesType: this data type is produced by the given method or built-in function.
Inverse of methodOf: a type or class has this method.
Inverse of throwsError: this error is raised by the given entity.
Inverse of requiresConcept: this concept is required by the given skill.
